title: W2L Evidence Record v1
description: The evidence W2L attaches to every scrape result (evidenceRecord), batch item and crawl page, stated the same way whichever lane produced it. Every field is always present; a value W2L did not observe is null, never 0 or a guess. The record sits beside the result's own fields and changes none of them. Versioning: w2l.evidence/1 changes only additively, so this file accepts every record an earlier revision of it accepted: a field added later is optional here (artifacts' bytes and contentType, added with file download; contentEncoding, added when the HTTP lane began decoding unrequested codings), though W2L writes it on every record from then on; enums only gain values; no field changes its meaning. A change that cannot follow this rule gets a new schemaVersion and a new schema file.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this schema. A record with another value follows another schema.

requestedUrl.description: The URL the caller asked for, as given.

finalUrl.description: The last URL W2L requested for the page, after following redirects: the URL of the response it reports, or of the request that got none (a timeout, a refused connection). On browser lanes a script or a meta refresh that loaded another document is a redirect; a URL the page set with the history API (pushState, replaceState), which nothing requested, is not. Null when W2L sent no request for the page: a robots.txt disallow, a DNS failure or a policy refusal came first.

redirectChain.description: Every URL W2L requested for the page, in order, and whether the lane lists every hop.

fetchedAt.description: When W2L received the response it reports, in UTC, ISO 8601 with milliseconds as JavaScript's Date#toISOString writes it: the final response's headers on the HTTP lane, the vendor's answer on the provider lane, the capture of the rendered page on browser lanes. Null when the result reports no response or the lane captured none (a browser-lane 503 left for a later retry), and on results stored before W2L recorded it.

httpStatus.description: The HTTP status of the response W2L reports, the one that answered finalUrl: on browser lanes, of the document the page shows when it is captured. Null when there was none; a browser navigation that reports no status is null too, never 0.

status.description: W2L's verdict on the page: the result's status. success and partial carry content; a failed or blocked result may carry the error page as evidence, never as content.

reason.description: Why the status is what it is: the failure reason when status is failed, the block reason when blocked, the exhausted budget when budget_exceeded. Null for every other status.

lane.description: The lane that produced the result: http (W2L's own HTTP client), browser_local (a local headless Chromium), browser_local_authed (the same with the user's session), browser_proxy (a browser through the operator's egress), provider (a third-party browser service) or my_browser (the person's own Chrome, on a site they allowed).

robotsDecision.description: The robots.txt verdict the page was fetched, or refused, under. Null when no robots.txt decision was made for this result: it ended before the check (a DNS failure, an identity refusal, a deadline), or robots.txt was not consulted.

rawSha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the body W2L read, the same value as evidence.rawBodySha256. For a file (a PDF, CSV, JSON, text, XLSX, XLS or ZIP response, listed in artifacts with kind file), in every lane: the SHA-256 of the bytes received, after any Content-Encoding was undone (see contentEncoding), equal to that artifact's sha256. For a web page on the HTTP lane: the response body, after any Content-Encoding was undone, decoded as text and encoded as UTF-8, which equals the SHA-256 of those bytes for a UTF-8 body without a byte-order mark. Browser lanes: the rendered page's HTML serialization, as UTF-8. Provider lane: the HTML the vendor returned, as UTF-8. Null when no body was read.

contentEncoding.description: The Content-Encoding of the response the body was read from, as the HTTP lane received it whether or not it asked for one: its codings lower-cased in the order applied, comma-separated (x-gzip read as gzip), or identity when the body was not encoded. The HTTP lane decodes gzip, deflate and br under the decompressed-size cap, so on a result with content it names what was decoded before rawSha256 was taken; any other coding fails the result with unsupported_content_encoding and is named here. Null when no body was read, and in the browser and provider lanes, which do not report it. Added to v1 after its first publication: optional here, written on every record from then on.

outputSha256.description: SHA-256 of what W2L delivered in this response, so that a cited value can be checked against it.

extractor.description: The extraction that turned the page into the delivered output.

fieldEvidence.description: For a JSON request: a JSON Pointer into json.data mapped to where that value was read. Every value has an entry: one read from the page (the content title included), one W2L took from the fetch itself (the URL), the page type W2L inferred, and one given by the model fallback. A field that is absent or null has none. An empty object when no value has one; null when JSON was not requested.

artifacts.description: Files W2L saved while producing this result, each with its SHA-256: a file response (PDF, CSV, ...) saved as received (kind file), and, when the operator sets W2L_CAPTURE_RAW_DIR, the page snapshot and the screenshot format's image. An empty list when nothing was saved.

proxy.description: host:port of the operator's environment proxy (HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY, local mode only) that the request for the final URL went through; never its credentials. Null when that request went direct, and whenever the lane reports no route for the result: when no request was sent, after a failed browser navigation, and on the provider lane.

identity.description: Who W2L said it was on the wire.

pageActions.description: The request's actions that ran on the page before it was read, in order, with their outcome; null when the request had none. rawSha256 and outputSha256 are of the page as the steps left it, and scriptRan says when a script of the caller's ran in it, so its content may be the script's. Added to v1 with the interaction group: optional here so that earlier records stay valid; W2L writes it on every record.

access.description: How the result was reached: the route, the client that sent its requests and the third-party spend of the run, read from the result's own trace (ADR 0005). Added to v1 with enhanced access: optional here so that earlier records stay valid; W2L writes it on every record.

urls.description: Every URL W2L requested for the page, in order: requestedUrl first, finalUrl last, with each redirect between (on browser lanes, a document a script or a meta refresh loaded is one). [requestedUrl] when there was no redirect; empty when W2L sent no request for the page (finalUrl is null).

complete.description: Whether the lane lists every hop. True on the HTTP lane, which follows redirects itself and requests each hop, and on the browser lane when it lists each redirect Chromium followed and each document a script or a meta refresh loaded; false there when a follow-up navigation did not start at requestedUrl, a document came without a request, or the chain of a page that kept moving on was cut to its first URL and last 20. False on the provider lane, which observes only where navigation started and where it ended: its list is [requestedUrl, finalUrl] after a redirect.

decision.description: allowed or disallowed by the robots.txt rules for the User-Agent of the request (on the provider lane, the vendor's); a robots.txt that could not be fetched counts as disallowed, see unreachable. no_robots when robots.txt was requested and the site has none (a 4xx, or a body that is not text/plain).

robotsUrl.description: The robots.txt URL consulted; null when it could not be located.

robotsSha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the robots.txt bytes parsed. Null when none were parsed (no robots.txt, or unreachable), and on results stored before W2L recorded it.

unreachable.description: Why robots.txt could not be fetched: server_error (a 5xx), network_error or timeout. RFC 9309 §2.3.1.4 then requires a complete disallow, so decision is disallowed. Null when robots.txt was fetched.

crawlDelayMs.description: The Crawl-delay robots.txt sets for W2L's User-Agent, in milliseconds; null when it sets none.

userOverride.description: Whether the fetch went ahead although decision is disallowed (a rule the publisher wrote, or an unreachable robots.txt); overrideBasis says on whose word. The result's trace (robots_overridden) and warnings, and in the browser lane its compliance record, carry the rule set aside, the reason and who recorded it. False otherwise, and always on results stored before W2L had the override.

overrideBasis.description: On whose word the disallow was set aside: robots_override, the caller's recorded robotsOverride or robotsOverrides entry; user_named_url, a local server fetching a URL the request named (a scrape, a batch entry), as robots.txt binds the links a crawl or map discovers; ignore_robots_txt, a crawl or map started with ignoreRobotsTxt on a local server. Null when nothing was set aside. Added after userOverride, so optional here; absent on results stored before it, where a true userOverride was a robots_override.

markdown.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the UTF-8 bytes of the markdown string exactly as delivered in this response (for a failed or blocked result, the error page kept as evidence). Null when no Markdown was delivered.

json.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the UTF-8 bytes of json.data as delivered, serialized as canonical JSON (RFC 8785: object keys sorted by UTF-16 code units at every level, no whitespace, strings and numbers as JSON.stringify writes them). Null when JSON was not requested or json.data is null.

name.description: The extractor: extract-tf, W2L's main-content extraction and Markdown conversion of web pages, which every lane uses; pdf-text for a PDF (its text layer, with a page marker before each page); file-text for another file (CSV, JSON and plain text as their text, XLSX, XLS and ZIP without text).

version.description: The extractor's version: EXTRACTOR_VERSION (for example extract-tf/1) for a web page, PDF_TEXT_VERSION (pdf-text/1) for a PDF, FILE_TEXT_VERSION (file-text/1) for another file. It changes whenever the Markdown produced from the same bytes can change.

commit.description: The W2L source commit that ran, as the operator declares it in W2L_SOURCE_COMMIT (7 to 40 hex digits). Null when not declared.

source.description: What the value was read from: jsonld, microdata, meta (a meta tag), hydration (the page's embedded application state), dom (the page's markup, including its own label/value rows, its first main-content heading and its <title>), text (visible prose), inferred (derived from context, such as a currency from the domain or the page type W2L classified), model (the configured model fallback), fetch (the fetch itself, not the page: its final or requested URL) or pdf (a Label: value line of a PDF's text).

locator.description: Where the value was read: a JSON Pointer or JSON-LD path, a CSS selector (title for the page's <title>), table[i] tr[j] "label" (dl[i] dt[j] "label") for a label/value row of the main content and h1[0] for its first heading, zero-based in document order; for fetch, the result field (finalUrl, requestedUrl); for inferred, the result field holding W2L's inference (document.pageType, document.product.kind); for pdf, page N "label", N being the page's 1-based position in the file (the <!-- page N --> marker in the Markdown). Null when the source gives no location: model, and for now JSON-LD, microdata and meta values outside the Amazon adapter, whose extraction does not record where it read them.

kind.description: snapshot: the page's HTML as W2L read it (the rendered page on browser lanes). file: a file response (PDF, CSV, JSON, text, XLSX, XLS, ZIP) saved byte for byte as received. screenshot: the browser lane's capture for the screenshot format, saved under W2L_CAPTURE_RAW_DIR as <sha256>.png or .jpg, with its size and type. Null when W2L cannot tell what the file is.

path.description: Where the file was saved, on the machine that ran W2L.

sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the file's bytes; null when unknown.

bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes: for kind file, every byte received. Null when unknown (a snapshot); for kind screenshot, the image's bytes. Added to v1 with file download: optional here so that earlier records stay valid; W2L writes it on every artifact.

contentType.description: The Content-Type header the file was received with, as sent. Null when the response sent none or W2L did not record it (a snapshot); for kind screenshot, image/png or image/jpeg. Added to v1 with file download: optional here so that earlier records stay valid; W2L writes it on every artifact.

userAgent.description: The User-Agent sent for the page, as observed: the header W2L sent on the HTTP lane, the header the browser sent on browser lanes, the User-Agent the vendor reports on the provider lane. Null when the lane did not observe it: the result ended before a request was made, the navigation failed, or the vendor did not report it.

mode.description: The crawl mode: research declares a bot (with the operator's contact when one is set), standard and authed present a consistent browser identity (authed with the user's session), proxy uses the operator's egress.

contact.description: The contact the research-mode User-Agent declares (W2L_CONTACT). Null when none is declared.

device.description: The device the answering lane's identity declared: mobile for a request with mobile true, else desktop. Null when W2L sent no request for the page, in research mode (a bot declares no device), or when the lane recorded none (the provider lane). Added to v1 with the cache group: optional here so that earlier records stay valid; W2L writes it on every record.

requestHeaders.description: The caller's custom request headers (the headers option) the answering lane sent, names lower-cased and sorted, each with the SHA-256 of its value and never the value itself (a value may be a key; the scrape record keeps names only). Empty when it sent none; null when W2L sent no request for the page. Credentials, transport headers and the declared identity (User-Agent, client hints) are refused before any request, so none is listed. Added to v1 with the cache group: optional here so that earlier records stay valid; W2L writes it on every record.

steps.description: The steps that ran, in the order given; a step that failed is the last.

scriptRan.description: Whether an executeJavascript step ran in the page.

outcome.description: ok, or failed (the steps after it did not run).

valueSha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the UTF-8 bytes of the value as sent.

route.description: The route that produced the result: http (W2L's HTTP client), http_compat (the browser-compatible HTTP transport, compatible_transport), browser (the local headless browser), enhanced_browser (the local browser on Patchright, enhanced_browser), authed_browser (the local browser with the user's saved login), user_browser (the person's own browser: after a handoff, or on the my_browser lane) or vendor (a third-party browser service). Null when no lane produced the result: the ladder's own answer for a rung the deadline cut, that failed or whose identity was refused, or a cache-only request that found nothing; nothing then says which client ran.

executor.description: The client that sent the requests: undici, impit, playwright, patchright, the person's browser as it named itself, or the vendor's id. Null when the result does not say (a vendor result without its vendor).

executorVersion.description: The executor's version as the lane reported it; null when it reported none.

profile.description: The browser profile the HTTP transport sent (impit's, for example chrome142); null on every other route. Its header set is in identity; its TLS fingerprint was not observed.

externalCostUsd.description: Third-party spend, in USD, of the run that produced the result (for a cache hit, of the fetch it reuses): 0 when no paid service was called, null when a called service stated no price. The egress (a person's own proxy) is not counted.

completion.description: How the page was read, counted apart: unattended (W2L's own lanes, no session of the person's), authorized_session (with the person's saved login), user_browser (in the person's own Chrome, on a site they allowed, without a step of theirs), handed_to_person (in their Chrome, after they got through a check). Null when no page was read. Added with the my-browser lane: optional here so that earlier records stay valid.
